decisionsTitle: The e2e specs write no date the calendar will reach
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-01**, after the review of BR-V3.98-2026-10-31: «Do them all». The item is the project's own note (`docs/QUEUE.md` «Later»): the e2e specs on written 2027 dates want a dates-from-today helper. About sixty written 2027 days in twenty-two spec files began to fail from 14–15 April 2027, one spec after another, as each date passed: an event in the past leaves the listing, its registration has closed and the signing of a group run's declaration shuts an hour after its start.

**Decision.** `tests/e2e/support/dates.ts`. A spec keeps its written date as a *pattern* and types `ahead("2027-05-04")`: the same day of the week a whole number of weeks later. There is one shift for the whole suite, the smallest that puts the earliest pattern (14 April 2027) 24 weeks ahead of today in Brașov — about as far ahead as it was when the specs were written — so a weekday a spec relies on (a Monday series with a Wednesday added), the gap between two of its dates (a series' end before its start, a second date a week later) and two dates written alike all stay true, and no registration window a spec opens has begun already. Today is read on the club's clock (`Europe/Bucharest`), not the machine's.

What a whole-week shift does not keep is derived, never written a second time: the calendar's `?month=` is `monthOf` of the typed day; the picker's `30.09.2027` is the typed day's own digits; an age typed against a run's limit (§561: the declaration's minimum age, a minor under 18) comes from `birthOn(runDay, age, daysUntilBirthday)`, because a written 1990 is a year older each time the run's day moves, and the line under the box (`Vineri, 11 mai 1990`) from `dayLine`; the night event, whose subject is the season (the sunset of a November evening against a June one), asks for `nextMonthDay(11, 17)` and reads the weekday and the year from `written`; and a race written straight into the database is written as a local time (`AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Bucharest'`), because a summer instant shifted into winter would read an hour early on the page. `seo.spec.ts` names a month inside the calendar's two-year window (`monthOf(ahead(...))`), because a month outside it is not a named period and would redirect to the bare calendar: the test still proves the named period page is canonical to `/ro/calendar`. The shift is read once per process, so a run that crosses the club's midnight fills and asserts the same day. A unit test (`tests/unit/events/e2e-dates.test.ts`) holds the helper across leap days, the year's end and the club's midnight, which is not UTC's.

**Refused.** Moving the written dates to 2031 by whole weeks: it would have worked for four years and been the same afternoon again, and a hand-edited year is the one fix no one remembers. A fake clock in the browser: the server renders the dates, and `test:clock` already moves the unit tests' clock. A seeded fixture event for every spec: the specs create their own events on purpose, as other specs unpublish the seeded ones.
changelogLine: - **The e2e specs no longer hold dates the calendar will reach** — `ahead()` in `tests/e2e/support/dates.ts` moves a written day by whole weeks so it is always months ahead with the same weekday and gaps, and the months, ages, seasons and offsets the specs read are derived from it; twenty-two specs from 14 April 2027 on stay green. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given an end-to-end spec that creates an event on a written day, when the calendar passes that day, then the spec still passes: it types the day through the suite's one helper, which moves a written date by whole weeks to at least 24 weeks ahead of today in Brașov — the same weekday, the same gaps between two dates, two equal dates still equal — and every month, age, season and clock offset the spec asserts is derived from that day, never written again (2026-11-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the e2e specs stop writing dates the calendar will reach
